title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-television
label: Mike 'The Biz' Bisignano
how: Pinfall, a frog splash off the top rope through a table (The Delmar Dive), after the wheel landed on Hardcore Rules.
note: Successfully defended against Blake Hamilton in a No Disqualification match on Prelude To Violence III, then in a ladder match against a masked enforcer for Valec Corso at Vegas Violence V, then again in a ladder match against Robbie Caldwell at Fear Is Coming II, before losing the title to Lark Fenriz inside the Rage In The Cage cage match at Phear Phantastic 2005 after a masked interloper (revealed afterward as Classy Joey Boy) struck both men with a canoe paddle.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-television
label: Lark Fenriz
how: Pinfall over Mike Bisignano inside the Rage In The Cage cage match, after a masked interloper (revealed afterward as Classy Joey Boy) struck both men with a canoe paddle from above.
note: Won as one of four falls inside a single ten-man cage match that also awarded a new fifth title and saw the 24 Hour Championship successfully defended. Retained on Winter War I against Justin Harper: Kagedo's own chair interference let Harper score an apparent pinfall, but promotion co-owner Rod Beauty overturned the result to a disqualification win for the champion. Lost the title to Harper on Winter War II inside a triple threat also involving Kagedo, when Kevin Simmons's own interference knocked Kagedo out cold and let Harper pin him for the title.

title: vxw-tag-team-championship
label: The O'Malley Brothers
how: Anthony O'Malley unhooked the suspended title belts while Stevie Knight fell from the other ladder, in a Tables Ladders and Chairs match, ending Hot Property's own reign.
note: The O'Malley Brothers' own first VXW Tag Team Championship win, after a No DQ Tornado loss to Wheeling's Thugs and a scored Irish Street Fight loss to the champions earlier in their own pursuit. Retained the titles in their first defense, against Team Brittania at St Patricks Day Massacre, on a disqualification after Anthony O'Malley struck Simon Davidson with a chair. Lost the titles to Team Brittania at The Hype III, Justin Davidson pinning Marcus O'Malley with the Kiss of Death after valet Kelly DeClair's own ringside interference.

title: vxw-24-hour-championship
label: Adam "The Hype" Jennings
how: Pinfall (the Hyperdrive, a reversal of Thunder Valenkov's own attempted Thunder Bomb) inside a Russian Cage Match.
note: Jennings's own first VXW Twenty-Four Hour Championship win, after a New Years Eve Of Destruction title match loss to Valenkov decided by Hot Property's own ringside interference. Retained the title in a rematch against Valenkov at St Patricks Day Massacre, pinning him with the Hyper Drive after the returning "Outlaw" Morris Bass's own interference backfired. Suspended and reported to have left for an outside opportunity sometime before Sin City Fights August 31; the title was declared vacant and contested across a mid-year tournament culminating at Vegas Violence 2006.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-television
label: Justin Harper
how: Pinfall over Kagedo, not champion Lark Fenriz, inside a triple threat, after Kevin Simmons's own interference knocked Kagedo out cold and Harper hit a Spinebuster on Fenriz before covering the fallen Kagedo for the three count.
note: Harper's own first title win in the held record. His own next match on record, against Roman Anderson on Winter War III, was explicitly billed non-title and is not treated as a defense. Retained the title in a scored Taipei Death Match against the same challenger, Roman Anderson, at St Patricks Day Massacre, a stipulation decreed by new 49 percent owner Lark Fenriz. Retained again in a twenty-minute time-limit draw against Omega at Hotter Than Hell I. Fought John Manning to a further time-limit draw at Sin City Fights August 31, in a match the broadcast's own commentary questioned the title status of after co-owner Spartacus's earlier title-stripping spree reportedly overlooked Harper; co-owner Ric Beauty publicly recognized Harper as champion on Sin City Fights September 19, setting a defense against Lance Voltar (winner of the TV Title Open Match's own Ring Two) at Vegas Violence. Retained again over 'The Big V' Lance Voltar at Vegas Violence 2006, opening the show with a Wipeout after kicking out of a top-rope corkscrew elbow.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-championship
label: Damian Payne
how: Pinfall over Justin Harper (a small package) inside the Rage In The Cage cage match, with Kagedo rolling through Harper's own attempted pin to put Payne on top.
note: The inaugural champion, in a title created on the spot for the first non-champion to pin another non-champion inside the same cage match. Retained the title against Omega on Christmas Comes Early in a Table For Two match, both men crashing through the same table together before the referee ruled Payne on top. Lost the title to Cobra at Xtreme Machine I, escaped from an escapes-only steel cage.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-television
label: Cobra
how: Pinfall over the beaten John Manning in a triple threat that also involved champion Justin Harper, after Roman Anderson, disguised as the match's own replacement referee, knocked Manning out with brass knuckles.
note: Cobra's first VXW Spin The Wheel Television Championship win, ending Justin Harper's own reign without Harper landing the deciding fall himself. Retained the title over Justin Davidson with the Snakebite at Sin City Fights November 18, after brother Simon Davidson's own ringside run-in with a cane broke Davidson's own focus. Contested again in the same three-way at New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, Miles McKinley eligible to win only this title from Cobra; the match ended without a decision when the referee called for the bell amid a mass brawl, Cobra still champion.

title: vxw-tag-team-championship
label: Team Brittania
how: Pinfall, Justin Davidson's Kiss of Death on Marcus O'Malley, after valet Kelly DeClair threw makeup in Marcus's eyes and low-blowed Anthony O'Malley from the apron.
note: Team Brittania's own first VXW Tag Team Championship win, after a four-way draw against champions Hot Property at Birthday Bash 2005 and a disqualification win over The O'Malley Brothers at St Patricks Day Massacre that did not change the title in their own earlier pursuit of it; wins the titles outright this time from The O'Malley Brothers, who had held them since Ghost Town Blues. Retained the titles in their first defense, against Purgatory at Hotter Than Hell I, on a disqualification after Synn accidentally kicked the referee. Lost the titles to The O'Malleys at Vegas Violence 2006 in a six-team scramble, Marcus O'Malley pinning Justin Davidson with a small package after Davidson nearly stole the title on a hot cover of a beaten-down Marcus.

title: vxw-24-hour-championship
label: Thunder Valenkov
how: Pinfall, a Thunder Bomb, for the title left vacant by Adam Jennings's own suspension, at the end of a mid-year tournament (a Second Chance Battle Royal and four quarterfinals narrowing to a Final Four, then a Vegas Violence final).
note: Valenkov's second documented VXW 24 Hour Championship win (this broadcast introduces him as 'the three time former 24 Hour Champion,' a claim the held record's documented history does not fully account for). Omega's own manager Richard Masterson secretly conspired with Valenkov's manager Chris Wheeling, saying something to Omega mid-match that left him open to the Thunder Bomb; Valenkov refused Wheeling's demand to attack the beaten Omega afterward. Manager Chris Wheeling wore the belt himself in a mock celebration and continued to lead Valenkov to the ring wearing it through Sin City Fights October 16 and October 24, without a title defense on either broadcast. Still without a defense, Wheeling gave Valenkov a night off from wearing the belt to the ring on Sin City Fights November 18 in order to wrestle a non-title match himself in Valenkov's place, then had Valenkov stand ringside without it again on Sin City Fights November 27. Contested again in a three-way match against Television Champion Cobra and challenger Miles McKinley at New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, under special rules barring Valenkov from losing the title to McKinley; the match ended without a decision when the referee called for the bell amid a mass brawl, Valenkov still champion.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-championship
label: Cobra
how: Cage escape inside an escapes-only steel cage match, pushing off with his boots to send Damian Payne backward through the open door.
note: Cobra's own first VXW Spin The Wheel Championship win, ending Damian Payne's own reign as the title's inaugural champion. Lost the title back to Payne at St Patricks Day Massacre.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-championship
label: Damian Payne
how: Pinfall, the Last Stop followed by a Chokebomb.
note: Payne's own second VXW Spin The Wheel Championship win, regaining the title he lost to Cobra twelve days earlier at Xtreme Machine I. Cobra repeatedly claimed the championship on air across the promotion's later broadcasts, defending it in matches billed as title defenses against Mr. Jones (The Hype II), Mr. Sal (The Hype IV) and John Manning (Hotter Than Hell I), but no surviving card ever bills or records a title change away from Payne. Payne remains this championship's last documented holder through the promotion's final surviving broadcast, Sin City Fights February 7, 2007, where he wrestles a non-title match unrelated to the championship.

title: vxw-tag-team-championship
label: The O'Malleys
how: Pinfall, Marcus O'Malley's small package on Justin Davidson, in a six-team scramble that also saw The Dierdorfs and Purgatory disqualified.
note: The O'Malleys' second VXW Tag Team Championship win (their own pre-match promo claimed a third reign overall, a count the held record's documented history does not fully support), ending Team Brittania's own reign at Vegas Violence 2006. A returning Blake Hamilton and Lance Voltar attacked the match's own last team standing, The Outlaw Morris Bass, moments before the finish. Lost the titles, together, when The Outlaw Morris Bass clotheslined Marcus and Anthony O'Malley through the two-story cage's own wall during Phear Phantastic 2006's own Rage In The Cage main event, pinning both men at once to claim both belts alone.

title: vxw-tag-team-championship
label: The Outlaw Morris Bass
how: Pinfall over both Marcus and Anthony O'Malley at once, clotheslining them together through the two-story cage's own wall to the arena floor during the Rage In The Cage main event.
note: The Outlaw Morris Bass's first VXW Tag Team Championship win, credited as a solo champion after the broadcast's own referee awarded him both title belts; revealed immediately afterward as an ally of a returning Kevin Simmons, who chair-shotted Marcus O'Malley from outside the ring. Retained by disqualification over The O'Malleys at Sin City Fights November 27 after Simmons again chair-shotted Marcus O'Malley, then helped Simmons put both O'Malleys down with a Durham Deathdrop and a Widowmaker after the bell. Lost the title to Roman Anderson and John Manning, billed afterward as The Outcasts, at New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, John Manning's schoolboy landing after a returning Adam Jennings distracted Bass from the entrance stage.

title: vxw-24-hour-championship
label: Thunder Valenkov

won.source: No document in the held record dates the start of this reign; the record opens with him already champion, defending against Robbie Caldwell at Birthday Bash 2005. The promotion's own broadcasts state, without naming a document, that Valenkov won the title from Adam Jennings and then defeated Robbie Caldwell for it in a triple threat match.

how: Unknown — the record opens with him already champion.
note: Defended successfully against Robbie Caldwell at Birthday Bash 2005 and against The Maquilladora on Prelude To Violence I, then again against The Maquilladora at Vegas Violence V in a match that ended the challenger's own career. Defended again on New Years Eve Of Destruction against Adam 'The Hype' Jennings, Hot Property's own ringside interference deciding the finish after the match's own first referee was knocked out. Lost the title to Adam Jennings on Ghost Town Blues inside a Russian Cage Match, Jennings pinning him with the Hyperdrive after reversing Valenkov's own Thunder Bomb.

title: vxw-spin-the-wheel-television
label: Valec Corso

won.source: No document in the held record dates the start of this reign; the record opens with him already champion on Xtreme Prejudice VI.

how: Unknown — the record opens with him already champion.
note: Lost the title to Mike Bisignano at Birthday Bash 2005 when a frog splash off the top rope drove him through a table.

title: vxw-tag-team-championship
label: The Outcasts
how: Pinfall, John Manning's schoolboy on champion 'The Outlaw' Morris Bass, after a returning Adam Jennings appeared on the entrance stage and distracted Bass mid-cover.
note: Roman Anderson and John Manning's own first VXW Tag Team Championship win, together billed afterward as The Outcasts, ending 'The Outlaw' Morris Bass's own solo reign. A Sin City Fights February 7 angle framed the returning Dierdorfs' own long pursuit of a title shot, but the bout it produced was fought as a non-title singles match between Anderson and Kris Dierdorf, which Anderson won by disqualification after Brian Dierdorf and valet Delila jumped into the ring; Manning cleared the ring afterward with his own title belt.

title: vxw-tag-team-championship
label: Hot Property

won.source: No document in the held record dates the start of this reign; the record opens with the team already champions, contended for by three teams on Xtreme Prejudice VII.

how: Unknown — the record opens with the team already champions.
note: Retained through a four-way draw against Team Brittania at Birthday Bash 2005, a defense against The Rhombus on Prelude To Violence I, and a three-way title match against Purgatory and Team Brittania at Vegas Violence V that ended by disqualification with no title change. Confirmed still champions on Setting Sun I after the promotion's own management publicly rejected a stripping rumor stemming from Austin Lee's own Rage In The Cage cover of his tag partner Stevie Knight at Phear Phantastic 2005, then survived a Tornado Tag Team title defense against The O'Malley Brothers on Christmas Comes Early that ended in a double-pin with no official decision rendered. Retained again on New Years Eve Of Destruction, beating The O'Malley Brothers 12-9 in a scored Irish Street Fight after two of Chris Wheeling's own hired men drove Marcus O'Malley through a table. Lost the title to the O'Malley Brothers on Ghost Town Blues in a Tables Ladders and Chairs match, Anthony O'Malley unhooking the belts while Stevie Knight fell from the other ladder.
